title: U.S. House · Arizona's 9th District
area: Western Arizona: all of La Paz County, most of Mohave County (including Bullhead City, Kingman and Lake Havasu City), most of Yuma County, and the western part of Maricopa County (including Buckeye, Surprise and Wickenburg).

context.text: Arizona's 9th is the most Republican district in the state, rated R+15 by the Cook Partisan Voting Index heading into 2026.

candidates.name: Paul Gosar
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative (since 2011; representing the 9th District since 2023)

summary.text: Paul Gosar is the Republican incumbent U.S. Representative for Arizona's 9th Congressional District. A dentist who ran a practice in Flagstaff, he was first elected to the House in 2010 with no prior political experience and is serving his seventh term. He serves on the Natural Resources and Oversight and Government Reform committees.

background.text: Born in Rock Springs, Wyoming, on November 27, 1958; raised in Pinedale, Wyoming, and graduated from Pinedale High School in 1977.
Earned a B.S. from Creighton University in 1981 and a D.D.S. from the university's dental school in 1985.

Worked as a dentist; his official bio says he owned his dental practice and was a small businessman in Flagstaff for 25 years before his election, and Wikipedia lists a Flagstaff practice from 1989 to 2010.
Served as president of the Arizona Dental Association from 2004 to 2005, according to Wikipedia.

First elected to the U.S. House in 2010 as a first-time candidate, defeating incumbent Rep. Ann Kirkpatrick in the 1st District; he moved to the newly created 4th District in 2012 and has represented the redrawn 9th District since 2023.

Serves on the House Committee on Natural Resources, where he chairs the Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations, and on the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform; he previously chaired the Congressional Western Caucus in the 115th and 116th Congresses.

On November 17, 2021, the House voted 223-207 to censure Gosar and remove him from his committee assignments over a video he posted depicting violence toward Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez; he said the action was an attack on his First Amendment right to speak out against illegal immigration and said he does not espouse violence.
Won re-election in 2024 with 65.3% of the vote over Democrat Quacy Smith, and advanced unopposed from the July 21, 2026 Republican primary with 79,336 votes.

priorities.text: Says securing the border and enforcing immigration law is among his top priorities, citing an “A+” career grade from NumbersUSA and a 100% career rating from the Federation for American Immigration Reform.
Says protecting Second Amendment rights is a top priority, citing an “A” career grade from the NRA and Gun Owners of America.
Says his priorities include simplifying the tax code, cutting federal spending, and reducing the national debt.

positions.summary: Says the federal government must enforce immigration law and secure the border, opposes amnesty, and has supported legislation to crack down on illegal immigration.
positions.quote: I want to be absolutely clear: I oppose the efforts to grant any sort of amnesty by executive fiat, and I oppose any efforts in Congress to grant amnesty to those who have broken our laws.

positions.summary: Says he will not support what he calls unconstitutional gun restriction laws and opposes efforts to restrict Second Amendment rights.
positions.quote: I will not support unconstitutional gun restriction laws. I will actively fight any attempt to undermine our Constitution and infringe upon the Second Amendment rights of law-abiding citizens.

positions.summary: Describes himself as an ardent supporter of Israel and lists votes for U.S. military aid and security cooperation with Israel, including the Israel Security Supplemental Appropriations Act of 2024.
positions.quote: I voted for and passed H.R. 6126, the Israel Security Supplemental Appropriations Act of 2024 with $14.3 billion in additional funding to help Israel fend of genocidal attacks from Hamas.

positions.summary: Says he believes life begins at conception, supports ending federal funding for Planned Parenthood, and welcomed the overturning of Roe v. Wade.
positions.quote: I believe that life begins at conception. For my efforts in Congress, I have a 100% lifetime rating from multiple pro-life organizations, including the Susan B. Anthony Pro-Life America and National Right to Life.

positions.summary: Says he will not vote to raise taxes and rejects the idea that top earners should pay more, favoring simplifying the tax code instead.
positions.quote: I reject the idea that people in the top tax brackets should be required to pay even more than they already do under the notion that they are “paying their fair share.”

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform (2025-2026), on the Federal Law Enforcement and Health Care and Financial Services subcommittees.
Serves on the House Committee on Natural Resources (2025-2026), on the Energy and Mineral Resources Subcommittee, and chairs the Oversight and Investigations Subcommittee.

candidates.researchNotes: Gosar has not completed a Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey for the 2026 cycle; no detailed 2026 platform statement was found within the research window beyond his committee record.

summary.text: Danielle "Dani" Sterbinsky is the Democratic nominee for Arizona's 9th Congressional District. Born in Austin, Texas, she has served in the U.S. Navy since 2015 and works in higher education advising and human resources. She describes herself as a Navy veteran, certified HR professional and mother, and is running on accountability, education and economic issues.

background.text: Born in Austin, Texas; has served in the U.S. Navy since 2015.
Earned a bachelor's degree from the University of Hawaii, West Oahu in 2019 and a graduate degree in Industrial-Organizational Psychology from Grand Canyon University in 2023.
Works as an academic advisor and is affiliated with the Society for Human Resource Management; describes herself as a certified HR professional.
Says her campaign priorities are term limits and reducing the influence of money in politics, fully funded public schools, and support for small businesses and rural job creation.
Advanced unopposed from the July 21, 2026 Democratic primary with 35,700 votes.

priorities.text: Supports congressional term limits and reducing the role of money in politics, saying she has signed a pledge supporting term limits.
Says Arizona's public schools need to be fully funded with smaller class sizes and modernized classrooms.
Says she would fight for small businesses and support job creation in rural communities.

positions.summary: Says she is committed to lowering prescription drug costs and making healthcare affordable, citing constituents who buy medication from Canada or Mexico because of cost.
positions.quote: These are hardworking Arizonans who should never have to look outside our country just to afford the medicine they need. Stories like these are why I'm committed to lowering prescription drug costs and making healthcare affordable at home.

summary.text: William Perry is an independent write-in candidate on the general-election ballot for Arizona's 9th Congressional District, listed as an Independent Party candidate.

candidates.name: G. Seville Hatch

summary.text: G. Seville Hatch is an independent write-in candidate on the general-election ballot for Arizona's 9th Congressional District and a telecommunications engineer and company founder.

background.text: Born in Dallas, Texas; attended Tempe High School and earned a bachelor's degree from the Motorola University Lab in 1983.

Career experience includes working as an engineer; in his Candidate Connection survey he describes himself as founder and CEO of ATCi, a satellite communications systems provider headquartered in Chandler, Arizona, which he says he took ownership of in 1992.

Has been affiliated with industry groups including the Society of Satellite Professionals, World Teleport Association and National Association of Broadcasters, and lists industry awards in his survey.
Is a write-in candidate on the November 3, 2026 general-election ballot as an independent.
